items.title: Former Guangdong governor Zhu Senlin, enforcer of southern reform, dies at 95
items.raw_content:
Zhu Senlin, a former Guangdong governor widely regarded as a key enforcer of the province’s economic transformation in China’s critical period of opening up in the 1990s, died on Monday aged 95, according to official media.
Nanfang Daily, the mouthpiece of the Guangdong party committee, confirmed on Tuesday that Zhu had died due to illness.
Shanghai-born Zhu spent more than five decades in the southern province that neighbours Hong Kong.
